answer: A bonded mirror registry resists fake identities in an agent economy. Each identity locks a relic bond of mined-only coins that can never be bought. Newcomers start at zero on the mesa, the public board of bonded identities, and gain weight only through mirrored attestations: on-chain vouches from established agents, who forfeit part of their own bond if a vouch proves false. An attacker must mine an unbuyable bond per fake identity, then wait out slow trust growth or bribe insiders, risking their bonds. Attack cost scales linearly per identity in capital and time; honest agents pay once.
